method.label: Split by the first coin flips

annotationRationale: Total probability combines the three first-flip cases. Independence supplies the case weights and uniform square model, whose favorable probability is computed from triangle areas.
sourceMethod: Followed the official three-case conditioning argument and replaced its auxiliary diagram with an explicit description and area calculation of the two corner triangles.

review.mathCheck: The three first-flip cases contribute (1/4)(1/2)=1/8, (1/2)(1/2)=1/4, and (1/4)(1/4)=1/16. The last conditional probability is the area of two disjoint triangles with legs 1/2. Their sum is 7/16, choice B; strict boundaries have zero continuous probability.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, originally worded adaptation of MAA solution 22 on pages 12–13. The coordinate inequalities and triangle dimensions reconstruct the official shaded-square figure without needing a separate drawing.
review.annotationCheck: The cases are exhaustive and disjoint, their weights use independence correctly, and endpoints and strict inequalities are handled. All selected nodes fit the worked method.
